name: PowerShell
description: Adversaries abuse PowerShell commands and scripts, often with encoded or obfuscated command lines, hidden windows and download cradles.

name: Windows Command Shell
description: Adversaries use cmd.exe to run commands, batch scripts and chains of utilities.

name: Visual Basic
description: VBScript or VBA macros executed via wscript, cscript or Office applications.

name: JavaScript
description: JScript or JavaScript executed via wscript, cscript or mshta.

name: Windows Management Instrumentation
description: WMI or wmic used to execute processes locally or on remote nodes.

name: Scheduled Task
description: Tasks created with schtasks or the Task Scheduler to run programs at logon, startup or on a schedule.

name: Service Execution
description: Programs executed by creating or modifying a Windows service, commonly by remote administration tools.

name: User Execution: Malicious File
description: A user opens a file such as an Office document that runs code.

name: Spearphishing Attachment
description: Malicious attachments delivered by email; Office spawning shells is a common follow-on signal.

name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
description: Programs registered under CurrentVersion Run or RunOnce keys or the startup folder to launch at logon.

name: Windows Service
description: New or modified Windows services used for persistence or privilege escalation.

name: WMI Event Subscription
description: WMI event filters and consumers used to trigger execution.

name: LSASS Memory
description: Reading or dumping lsass.exe process memory to obtain credentials, e.g. via process access with read rights or minidump utilities.

name: Security Account Manager
description: Extracting the SAM hive to obtain local account hashes.

name: NTDS
description: Extracting the Active Directory database from domain controllers.

name: Brute Force
description: Repeated authentication attempts to guess passwords.

name: Credentials from Password Stores
description: Reading credentials from browsers or credential managers.

name: Obfuscated Files or Information
description: Encoding, packing or obfuscating payloads and command lines, such as base64-encoded PowerShell.

name: Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information
description: Decoding payloads on the host, for example with certutil -decode.

name: Regsvr32
description: Proxy execution of code through regsvr32.exe, including remote scriptlets.

name: Rundll32
description: Proxy execution of DLL exports or scripts through rundll32.exe.

name: Mshta
description: Proxy execution of HTA or script content through mshta.exe.

name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Name or Location
description: Malicious files or tasks named or placed to look like legitimate software.

name: Clear Windows Event Logs
description: Clearing event logs to remove evidence.

name: Disable or Modify Tools
description: Disabling or tampering with security tools such as antivirus.

name: Process Injection
description: Injecting code into the memory of other processes.

name: Modify Registry
description: Changing registry keys to hide configuration or enable execution.

name: Ingress Tool Transfer
description: Downloading tools or payloads onto the host, e.g. with PowerShell WebClient, certutil, bitsadmin or curl.

name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
description: Command and control over HTTP or HTTPS.

name: Application Layer Protocol: DNS
description: Command and control over DNS queries.

name: Encrypted Channel
description: Encrypted command and control traffic.

name: System Owner/User Discovery
description: Identifying the current user, e.g. whoami or quser.

name: Account Discovery
description: Enumerating local or domain accounts, e.g. net user or net group.

name: Domain Account Discovery
description: Enumerating domain accounts and groups.

name: System Network Configuration Discovery
description: Gathering network configuration, e.g. ipconfig, route, arp.

name: System Information Discovery
description: Gathering OS and hardware details, e.g. systeminfo.

name: Domain Trust Discovery
description: Enumerating domain trusts, e.g. nltest /domain_trusts.

name: Remote System Discovery
description: Listing other hosts on the network.

name: Process Discovery
description: Listing running processes, e.g. tasklist.

name: Remote Desktop Protocol
description: Logging on to remote hosts over RDP.

name: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
description: Using admin shares such as ADMIN$ or C$ to move laterally, often with service creation.

name: Windows Remote Management
description: Remote execution through WinRM or PowerShell remoting.

name: Archive Collected Data
description: Compressing or encrypting collected data before exfiltration.

name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
description: Sending data out over the command and control channel.

name: Data Encrypted for Impact
description: Encrypting files to disrupt availability, as ransomware does.

name: Inhibit System Recovery
description: Deleting shadow copies or backups.
